work_order.debate_summary: The critique was right on five majors and I rewrote the plan around them: (1) the [id]/loading.tsx boundary would wrap the editor routes, so the work order adds a minimal expenses/loading.tsx boundary; (2) server-rendered Today/Yesterday uses the server clock, so relative labels move to a client ExpenseDate island with a zone-neutral server first paint; (3) the UTC-labelled first paint re-ships exactly what ui.md bans, so first paints are zone-neutral absolute dates; (4) the excerpt diagnosis was factually right but the prescription (keep the full group feed with chips on the group page) contradicts IAC-2 and the issue's own 'activity-excerpt reads' contract, so the excerpt stays and the scope loss is fixed the other way with a ?group= filter on /activity applied in the page; (5) payer-coloured row totals assert a direction the ledger does not support, so row amounts render in ink with payer words and colour is reserved for real nets. Minor findings adopted: disclosure open-inline on desktop with active filters on the summary, Timestamp moved to a neutral components/timestamp.tsx module, app/activity/page.tsx named in files[], the missing validation test path supplied, a '+N more' overflow link on the summary, and loading tests pinned on the streamed Flight fallback per the QA environment notes. Dismissed: renaming lucide icon imports (unverified without node_modules; package.json confirms the dependency and the build is the check), and keeping chips plus the full filterable feed inside the Activity tab (the issue and ui.md both specify an excerpt linking out). Residual no-JS disclosure re-collapse and feed-row reflow after mount are recorded as risks, not silently dropped.

issue_snapshot.title: Group page with sections, expenses list and settings entry
issue_snapshot.body:
A group member finds the balance, the expenses, and the next action without scrolling one long stack, with Add expense always one tap away.

UI face: group member sees one organised page (summary plus tabbed Expenses, Balances and settle up, Activity, Members) with Add expense always reachable and settings tucked behind Settings. Contract face: consumes shell, tokens, rows, cards, segmented control, dialogs, and skeletons from piece 1; reuses existing group, expense-list, balance, and activity-excerpt reads with no endpoint or schema change. Follows docs/ui.md Group page structure and states exactly.

**Out of scope**
- Expense editor form internals and settle-up sheet internals (next piece)
- Balance-math, simplification, filter semantics, or activity-writing changes
- Dark mode

Covers: TR-11, S-8
Part of #31.
Depends on #33.

## Acceptance (from the split)
- **IAC-1** Group page shows shell with back-to-Home breadcrumb, group header (mark, name, currency badge, Settings entry), and a summary card with the user balance as hero number, who-owes-whom lines, primary Add expense and secondary Settle up.
- **IAC-2** Sections render as tabs or segmented control: Expenses, Balances and settle up, Activity excerpt linking to the full feed, Members excerpt linking to members; settings (rename, archive) live behind the Settings entry, never on the main scroll.
- **IAC-3** Expenses section shows newest-first rows (avatar left, title plus human-date metadata middle, amount right with words-plus-colour) with search plus member and category filters inside a disclosure on phones.
- **IAC-4** Row actions live in an overflow menu (edit, delete with confirm naming the expense); no inline Edit or red Delete buttons on rows; destructive choices confirm in a dialog or sheet.
- **IAC-5** Add expense is always reachable: header button on desktop and fixed bottom button on phones; empty group shows what-to-do-first with an Add-expense button and a settled banner when all balances are zero.
- **IAC-6** Loading shows skeleton summary card, section tabs, and three expense rows with no layout shift; a failed section shows inline retry inside its own panel; full failure shows a page error with retry, never a half-rendered ledger.
- **IAC-7** Dates read as people say them and times render in the viewer zone; works at 375px and 1280px (desktop may place summary in a side card); keyboard, focus, headings, and reduced-motion rules from ui.md hold.

Record the redesign as a new ADR.
